"Ripped" is a versatile word. Depending on the context — what situation it is used in — it can carry very different meanings. Here are all its key meanings as an adjective:

This is the most basic, literal meaning. When something made of fabric, paper, or a similar material has been forcefully torn or cut, it is described as ripped.

Examples:

  • "He was wearing ripped jeans." (jeans with tears in them)
  • "She pulled a ripped page out of her notebook."
  • "The ripped packaging told us the box had been opened before."

Key idea: The object has a tear or cut that makes it look damaged or broken apart.
2. Having a Very Muscular, Well-Defined Body

This is a very popular informal (slang) use, especially in fitness and gym culture. When a person has very visible, well-defined muscles — usually because they have very low body fat — they are called ripped.

Think of it this way: the muscles look so defined that they appear almost "cut out" or "carved," like a sculpted figure.

Examples:

  • "After training for a year, he was absolutely ripped."
  • "She has a ripped physique from years of weightlifting."

Key idea: The person's muscles are so defined and visible that their body looks extremely lean and powerful. It is a strong compliment in fitness culture.
3. Very Drunk or High on Drugs

In informal, conversational slang — especially common among younger people — ripped means being extremely intoxicated, either from alcohol or drugs.

Examples:

  • "They came home completely ripped after the party."
  • "He got ripped and couldn't remember anything the next morning."

Key idea: The person is so heavily under the influence that their normal state of mind has been, in a sense, "torn apart" from their usual self.

In the world of technology, ripped describes digital content — like music, movies, or audio — that has been copied from a physical source (like a CD or DVD) or extracted from a streaming service into a file on a computer.

Examples:

  • "He listened to a ripped version of the album."
  • "The ripped audio file was saved on his hard drive."

Key idea: The content has been "pulled out" or extracted from its original source and saved in a new format.
How to Always Know Which Meaning Is Intended

Since "ripped" has multiple meanings, context is everything. Here is a simple guide:

  • Talking about clothing or paper? → Torn/damaged.
  • Talking about someone's body or appearance? → Very muscular.
  • Talking about someone at a party or after drinking/drugs? → Very intoxicated.
  • Talking about music, movies, or files? → Digitally copied.

In all its meanings, "ripped" carries a sense of intensity and extremity. Jeans aren't just slightly worn — they're ripped. A person isn't just fit — they're ripped. Someone isn't just a little drunk — they're ripped. The word always suggests something taken to a strong degree.
